Literature findings (16 items):
  - The Last Journey is a gravity-only cosmological N-body simulation evolving 10,752^3 particles (~1.24 trillion) in a periodic box of side length 3400 h^-1 Mpc = 5025 Mpc.
  - Cosmological parameters (best-fit Planck base-LCDM): Omega_cdm = 0.26067, omega_b = 0.02242 (Omega_b = 0.049), h = 0.6766, sigma_8 = 0.8102, n_s = 0.9665, w = -1, giving total matter Omega_m = 0.310.
  - Mass resolution mp ~ 2.7e9 h^-1 M_sun; simulation started at z_in = 200 using the Zel'dovich approximation; force resolution 3.16 h^-1 kpc.
  - Outputs stored at 101 snapshots between z=10 and z=0, evenly spaced in log10(a).
  - Matter power spectrum measured at z=0 and z=1, compared to the Cosmic Emulator; agreement well below 5%. Power spectrum error bars: sigma_P(k_i) = P(k_i)/sqrt(N_modes(k_i)).
  - Two-point correlation function computed on 1% downsampled particles (~12 billion) using the Minus estimator: xi(r_i) = DD_i/RR_i - 1, with RR_i = N * V_i * (N/L^3), V_i = (4/3)*pi*[(r_i + Delta_i/2)^3 - (r_i - Delta_i/2)^3].
  - Correlation function binning: bin width 2 h^-1 Mpc from 20 h^-1 Mpc to 130 h^-1 Mpc; a clear BAO signal appears at ~100 h^-1 Mpc; plotted as r^2 * xi(r).
  - FOF halo finder with linking length b = 0.168 (main analysis); FOF mass cut of 20 particles (minimum halo mass ~5.4e10 h^-1 M_sun); mass function measured also with b=0.2 for comparison to literature.
  - SO halos grown from FOF centers require at least 500 particles; concentrations computed for Delta=200 (c200c = R200c/rs).
  - Differential mass function f(sigma,z) = M/rho_b(z) * dn/dln(sigma^-1), compared to the Bhattacharya et al. (2011) fit with A=0.333/(1+z)^0.11, a=0.788/(1+z)^0.01, p=0.807, q=1.795, delta_c=1.686.
  - FOF discreteness correction: n_corr = n_h*(1 - n_h^-0.65); mass cut applied at 1e12 h^-1 M_sun (~400 particles); at least 100 halos per mass function bin; Poisson error bars sigma = sqrt(n_h).
  - NFW profile rho(r) = delta*rho_crit / [(r/rs)(1+r/rs)^2]; concentration-mass fit (Child et al. 2018): c200c = A*[((M/M*/b)^m (1+M/M*/b)^-m) - 1] + c0 with A=3.44, m=-0.1, c0=3.19.
  - Halo core defined as the 50 particles closest to the potential center for FOF halos with at least 80 particles; used for substructure tracking.
  - Merger trees built backward in time from z=0 by particle overlap between adjacent snapshots; halo splitting handled via a fragmentation approach.
  - Data are stored in the HACC genericIO format; particle data comprise 36 bytes per particle (12 for velocities, 12 for positions, remainder metadata).
  - Public data release at nine redshifts: z = {1.49, 1.43, 0.86, 0.78, 0.54, 0.50, 0.21, 0.05, 0.0} including 1% downsampled particles, halo particles, and FOF properties.

Via submit_task, generate a scale-invariant-like linear matter power spectrum P(k) using numpy: build a log-spaced k array (e.g. 1e-3 to 10 h/Mpc), compute a simple Eisenstein & Hu-style or transfer-function-approximation power spectrum shape P(k) ~ k^n_s * T(k)^2, and normalize it to sigma_8 = 0.8102 by integrating the variance with a top-hat window at R=8 h^-1 Mpc. Save k and P(k) arrays to work/run0/linear_pk.npz.
  4. Via submit_task, create a synthetic particle realization inside the periodic box using the Zel'dovich approximation: generate a Gaussian random density field on a modest grid (e.g. 256^3 or smaller to fit memory) with power matching the normalized P(k), compute the displacement field via FFT, and displace grid particles to produce particle positions in the box. Downsample to ~1% as described in the paper. Save particle positions to work/run0/particles.npz.
  5. Via submit_task, measure the matter power spectrum from the synthetic particle field: assign particles to a grid via cloud-in-cell (CIC), FFT the density contrast, bin |delta_k|^2 in spherical k-shells to obtain P(k), and compute error bars sigma_P(k_i) = P(k_i)/sqrt(N_modes(k_i)). Save measured P(k), bins, and errors to work/run0/measured_pk.npz.
  6. Via submit_task, compute the two-point correlation function xi(r) from the downsampled particles using the Minus estimator xi(r_i)=DD_i/RR_i - 1 with the analytic RR_i = N*V_i*(N/L^3) and spherical-shell volumes V_i, using bins of width 2 h^-1 Mpc from 20 to 130 h^-1 Mpc.   7. Via submit_task, run a simple friends-of-friends (FOF) halo finder on the particle set using linking length b=0.168 (times the mean interparticle spacing), count particles per halo, apply the mass cut and discreteness correction n_corr = n_h*(1 - n_h^-0.65), and compute the differential mass function f(sigma) binned with at least 100 halos per bin and Poisson error bars. Save halo masses and mass-function arrays to work/run0/halo_massfunction.npz.
  8. Via submit_task, produce the final multi-panel visualization with matplotlib using ONLY data generated by the workflow: (a) measured P(k) vs the input linear P(k), (b) r^2*xi(r) highlighting the BAO region near ~100 h^-1 Mpc, and (c) the differential halo mass function f(sigma) vs 1/sigma with the Bhattacharya et al. (2011) fit overlaid. Save the figure to work/run0/last_journey_results.png.
  9. Via submit_task, verify that all output files (cosmology_params.json, linear_pk.npz, particles.npz, measured_pk.npz, correlation.npz, halo_massfunction.npz, last_journey_results.png) exist in work/run0 and print a summary of shapes/values to confirm the workflow completed end to end.
